why.stone: Strong faceting on bowls and digits reads as cut stone, comparable to the most carved variants.
why.carving: Facets are mostly coherent, but the rotated-diamond period and slightly uneven segment lengths on 6 and 5 feel more mechanical than chiselled.
why.calm: Steady overall, though the diamond dots and harder corners add a touch of nervousness.

why.stone: Clearly faceted curves across all letters and figures give a convincing hewn-inscription character.
why.carving: One consistent cutting logic with crisp straight planes and legible digits; only marginally rough on the heaviest bold rounds.
why.calm: Grounded and steady, though the pronounced facets make the bold numbers a touch more forceful than K1.

why.stone: The most convincingly hewn: angular bowls, faceted counters and diamond-like dots read as an inscription cut into stone.
why.carving: The faceting is one coherent system carried through letters, digits and punctuation, with digits easy to tell apart, though the largest bowls get somewhat coarse.
why.calm: Grounded with strong presence; the angularity is firm but not aggressive.

why.stone: Moderate faceting on bowls (O, 6, 0, B) gives a hint of hewn edges, but at a glance it still reads mostly as a smooth book serif.
why.carving: Facets are applied consistently across letters and digits with clean straight cuts, and 1/7, 3/8, 0/O stay clearly distinct.
why.calm: Quiet and steady with full presence; the cuts never call attention to themselves.

why.stone: Moderate polygonal faceting on bowls and curves gives the serif a hewn, inscribed feel without losing its classical shape.
why.carving: Facets are applied consistently across lowercase, caps and digits and stay crisp; 1/7, 3/8 and 0/O remain easy to tell apart, though the cuts are less decisive than in the stronger variants.
why.calm: Steady and composed, with enough texture to give presence without any agitation.

why.stone: Moderate faceting on bowls (B, e, 6, O) gives a hewn, inscriptional feel over a classical serif skeleton.
why.carving: Facets are applied evenly across letters and digits and stay crisp, with 1/7, 3/8 and 0/O clearly distinct, though some curves read slightly polygonal.
why.calm: Steady and grounded with good presence; the facets add a little edge but nothing shouts.

why.stone: Pronounced, even polygonal cuts on O, 0, 6, 5 and the lowercase bowls give a clear hewn-inscription feel.
why.carving: Faceting is consistent across the whole set with crisp planes and a round-ish period, and confusable digits remain easy to separate.
why.calm: Grounded and composed with presence, slightly more insistent than the subtler variants.

why.stone: Strong polygonal cuts on bowls and terminals read unmistakably as chiselled stone.
why.carving: Consistent in concept, but the bold rounds (O, 0, C, 6) show slightly irregular, stepped facets that start to look rough rather than precisely cut.
why.calm: Not aggressive, but the heavier faceting adds some restlessness to the bold display lines.

why.stone: Clear, medium-strength facets give a carved feel similar to K1.
why.carving: Facets are consistent and crisp across letters and figures with no broken shapes, and the digit pairs stay distinct.
why.calm: Balanced and steady, with presence and only mild angular tension.

why.stone: Clearly polygonal bowls on O, 6, 5, e and s read as chisel-cut planes, giving the titles and set numbers a convincing inscribed feel.
why.carving: One coherent faceting system across caps, lowercase and digits with crisp cuts; only some small bowls (s, e at the largest size) get slightly lumpy, and digits stay legible.
why.calm: Still composed, though the visible angularity adds a little more edge than the softer variants.

why.stone: Strong faceting turns every bowl into chiselled planes, so the display text reads clearly as cut stone.
why.carving: Coherent across the set, but at bold caps the O, C and 0 edges get slightly jagged and stepped, edging toward a rough rather than clean chisel.
why.calm: Still measured, but the rougher faceting adds a little visual noise at large bold sizes.

why.stone: Strong, visible facets on every bowl make the display text read clearly as cut stone.
why.carving: Facets are coarse and large enough that curves (e, s, 6, 5) start to look low-poly rather than chiselled, though digits remain distinguishable.
why.calm: Calm overall, but the heavier angularity adds some visual noise at large sizes.

why.stone: Faceting is so faint it is barely noticeable even at the largest size, so it reads as an ordinary serif.
why.carving: What carving there is is coherent and clean, but it is too subtle to register at display size.
why.calm: Very calm and balanced with solid presence.

why.stone: Faceting is subtle and mostly visible only on large curves, so it hints at stone more than it declares it.
why.carving: What carving there is looks clean and consistent, but it is so faint at display size that it barely registers as a design trait.
why.calm: Very calm and even, close to a plain classical serif, with solid presence from the weight.

why.stone: Faceting is subtle and mostly reads as a classical serif with only a hint of cut stone.
why.carving: What carving there is is clean and consistent, but it is barely visible at display size so it contributes little.
why.calm: Very calm and composed with full presence, close to a refined book serif.
